clue.text: Learner seeming, when not having answer, to freeze

indicators.note: the phrase tells us a letter is lost from the synonym for seeming

parts.note: something seeming is apparent
to freeze is to ice, as with a cake or a road

explanation.surface: Someone learning appears to freeze up when unable to answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when not having answer' takes one A out of the word for seeming, leaving APPRENT; 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee learning a trade under a master is a learner in that craft.

clue.text: Lack resolution, with loss of wicket, to declare

indicators.note: the phrase tells us a letter is dropped from the word for lacking resolution

parts.note: to waver is to be undecided
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A batsman losing a wicket wavers over whether to declare the innings closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with loss of' takes W out of WAVER. 'Declare' is a cricket term too, closing an innings, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: To state firmly is to assert, a direct synonym of declaring.

clue.text: Religious exercises for churchwarden?

parts.note: PI is short for pious, so religious
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Asks whether a churchwarden's duties include religious exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: A churchwarden is also a long-stemmed clay tobacco pipe; the question mark flags the second sense behind the church officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchwarden is a long clay smoking implement named after the parish officers who used them.

clue.text: Historian's done unusually absorbing book — great extract coming up

indicators.note: absorbing means the rearranged letters take the following pieces inside them
unusually means the letters of done are arranged in a new order

parts.note: the four letters are rearranged

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: great means big
to extract is to draw, as a tooth or water

explanation.surface: A historian's book, unusually done, holds a great extract on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges the four letters to sit either side; 'coming up' reverses the great extract to WARDGIB. Gibbon wrote The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Gibbon was the eighteenth-century English author of a famous history of Rome's decline; the 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: Short time before wrapping last of presents

indicators.note: wrapping means the word for before goes around the next piece

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: last of means we take the final letter of presents

explanation.surface: Little time is left before the last of the presents is wrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' gives S from presents; 'wrapping' puts ERE around it to make ERSE after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Curt, brief speech is short and to the point.

clue.text: Deceptions beloved of merchant's friend wanting power in associations

parts.note: cons are swindles or deceptions

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice, Antonio the merchant's friend Bassanio loves Portia
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Tricks beloved by a trader's companion fail without power in business groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting power' removes P from PORTIA, leaving ORTIA. The merchant is Shakespeare's Antonio, whose friend Bassanio wins Portia.
explanation.definitionFit: Consortia are partnerships of companies or bodies, so associations formed for a joint purpose.

clue.text: Sympathetic treatment involving a perfumed powder

indicators.note: involving means the abbreviation surrounds the article

parts.note: TLC is tender loving care

explanation.surface: Gentle care that includes dusting with scented powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts A inside TLC.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum is the scented dusting product applied after a bath.

clue.text: Like man with part in hood's crooked organisation

indicators.note: a crooked organisation of the words means their letters are set out in a twisted new order

parts.note: the ten letters of these words, the possessive adding none, are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hoodlum plays a role in a gangster's corrupt outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hood' as in hoodlum and 'crooked organisation' paint a gang, but they signal an anagram of PART IN HOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropoid apes resemble humans, so the word means resembling a human being.

clue.text: Firm track around a hollow in hill

indicators.note: around means the abbreviation for firm surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a pit is a hollow in the ground
a line is a railway track

explanation.surface: A company lays railway track round a dip in a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Capitoline is one of the seven hills of Rome; 'in' only links the wordplay to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Capitoline is the Roman summit where the temple of Jupiter stood.

clue.text: Block caused by crocks going west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means read from right to left

parts.note: crocks are earthenware pots

explanation.surface: A blockage caused by broken-down old wrecks heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crocks' suggests worn-out people or cars; here it means earthenware pots.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt or obstruct something is to block it.

clue.text: Force stopped by obstacle number raised with energy, letting nothing through

indicators.note: stopped by means the word for force is plugged by the next pieces

parts.note: to impel is to force or drive

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: a bar is an obstacle
ten is a number
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A force held back by a barrier, with energy, lets nothing pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses obstacle and number as one run, NETRAB, and 'stopped by' plugs that into the word for force before its final L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be passed or penetrated lets nothing get in.

clue.text: Honour obtained by anarchic trio, reformed

indicators.note: anarchic means disorderly, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written as part of the letter pool

explanation.surface: A distinction won by three rebels who have since reformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder: 'anarchic' rearranges TRIO REFORMED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Order of Merit is a British award given personally by the monarch for distinguished service.

clue.text: Items of lingerie, loads displayed as 'essentials'

parts.note: bras are items of underwear
stacks means loads, lots

explanation.surface: Underwear piled high is shown as the basics.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting down to brass tacks means dealing with the basic facts.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the basic facts or fundamentals of a matter.

clue.text: Prompt document from debtor, artful in bogus manner

parts.note: to spur is to prompt or urge
an IOU is a written promise from someone who owes money
sly means artful or cunning

explanation.surface: A cunning debtor's note pressing for payment is fake.
explanation.walkthrough: IOU stands for 'I owe you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsely or fraudulently, like counterfeit goods.

clue.text: Unacceptable ruling? Get up after reflection to break it

indicators.note: to break it means the reversed piece splits the word for ruling

parts.note: regnant means reigning or ruling

indicators.note: after reflection means the word up is seen as in a mirror, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks whether a ruling is unacceptable, then says to stand up after thinking and break it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after reflection' gives PU, which 'to break it' sets inside the word for ruling; 'Get' and 'it' only link, and the question mark flags 'ruling' as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repellent or offensive is unacceptable.

clue.text: Sign one ought to change, receiving censure

parts.note: A means one, as in a single item

indicators.note: receiving means the rearranged letters take in the word for censure
to change means the letters of ought are rearranged

parts.note: a rap is a rebuke or censure

explanation.surface: A signal that someone ought to change after being criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' gives UTOGH, and 'receiving' sets the censure inside it before the final H.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature, especially a celebrity's written for a fan, is what one signs.

clue.text: entering river, then lake

clue.text: Abandon land covered with low trees

explanation.surface: Giving up on ground thick with stunted woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap a plan is to call it off; also brushwood, stunted vegetation on poor ground.

clue.text: Adviser with good skill going round with new player

indicators.note: going round means the three pieces are turned about and read backwards

parts.note: an aide is an assistant or adviser
art means skill

explanation.surface: A counsellor with fine skill circles round a new actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' turns the three pieces round together as one run, giving TRAGEDIA before N.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor who specialises in tragic roles, so a stage performer.

clue.text: Love: not smooth, much getting in the way

indicators.note: getting in means these pieces go inside the word the

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis
rough means not smooth
far means much, as in far better

explanation.surface: Love is never smooth, with so much standing in its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting in' sets the pieces inside 'the'. The surface echoes Shakespeare's 'the course of true love never did run smooth'.
explanation.definitionFit: A main road or public route through a place is a way.

clue.text: Take off rook and mock

parts.note: to take off is to run away, flee
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A rook takes flight and jeers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' can mean mimic and mock, but here it means run away.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleer is an old word for to laugh scornfully or jeer.

clue.text: Paper tiger's jaunty

indicators.note: the 's after tiger stands for has: the phrase has the letters within it

explanation.surface: A harmless paper tiger looks cheerfully brash.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the join of 'Paper' and 'tiger'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pert means lively and sprightly, as a jaunty hat is.

clue.text: Garden seed meant to have odd pieces sifted out

indicators.text: to have odd pieces sifted out
indicators.note: removing the odd-numbered letters leaves only the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: Seed for the garden is to be sieved of odd bits.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 of 'seed meant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the biblical paradise garden of Adam and Eve.

clue.text: Money around? Stow it!

parts.note: CA is circa, about or around
stow it is slang for shut up, and SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A demand to keep quiet when money is about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stow it!' is British slang for 'be quiet', the same job as SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready coins and notes are money.

clue.text: Young man comprehending part of speech on a Welsh course?

indicators.note: comprehending means including, so the word for young man contains the following pieces

parts.note: a lad is a young man
a verb is a part of speech
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A boy who understands grammar on a Welsh language course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests study, but it is a course of a meal: laverbread is a Welsh dish made from seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Laverbread is boiled seaweed eaten in Wales, so one dish of a meal there; the question mark marks the trick.

clue.text: Small and yet oddly irritating thing on lid

indicators.note: oddly means the letters of yet are set in a strange new order

explanation.surface: Something small yet strangely annoying on an eyelid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges YET to TYE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling at the edge of the eyelid.

clue.text: Reveal entertaining bit of scandal following tea dance

indicators.note: following means the later pieces come after the word for tea

parts.note: char is British slang for tea

indicators.note: entertaining means holding, so the word for reveal contains a letter

parts.note: to let on is to reveal a secret

indicators.note: bit of means just the first letter of scandal

explanation.surface: Someone spills a juicy bit of gossip after a tea dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts S inside LET ON. 'tea dance' looks like one phrase; split it into 'tea' and 'dance'. The Charleston is a 1920s dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charleston is a lively jazz-age step with kicking legs.
